query:
Industry: precision machine repair workshop
Client brief: A precision machine repair workshop for local manufacturers. Show supported machine types and a repair enquiry. White and black only, Helvetica only, no animation, no invented accreditation.
Heading font: Helvetica
Body font: Helvetica
Brand colours: #FFFFFF, #111111, #666666
No animation.
No invented accreditation.

matched_industry.name: Artisan, Craft & Maker Commerce
matched_industry.layout_archetype: Object-led storefront: the made thing and the making process share the first viewport, then collection, classes/commissions, and maker story
matched_industry.first_viewport_priority: The actual object (drawn or photographed), who makes it and where, and one buy action plus one visit/book action

typography_pairing.mood: The brief's own type (Helvetica); scale and roles from bricolage-hanken

palette.notes: Brief colours #FFFFFF, #111111, #666666 lead: #FFFFFF is the ground; #666666 as accents; #111111 as surfaces and deep tones, never accents | base Starting point only: replace accents with colours sampled from the maker's own materials, glazes, dyes, or place (see `distinctiveness`)

conversion_trust_elements: Maker name, place, and process shown, not claimed
Honest batch size, lead time, and care/food-safety notes
Real seat/stock counts for classes and limited runs
matched_industry.motion_language: Slow, material motion (a turning wheel, a glaze sheen) used once as a signature; everything else quiet and fast
anti_patterns: Cream background + terracotta accent + italic serif headline (the default 'craft' look every generator produces)
Stock-photo hands-on-clay hero with no actual product
Rotating circular text badge and process-word marquee as filler

category_cliches: Cream/oatmeal background with a terracotta accent
Italic high-contrast serif headline (Fraunces / Playfair italic) with one coloured italic word
Arched image frame, rotating circular text badge, process-word marquee strip
Giant faint wordmark in the footer
distinctiveness.instruction: Subject first: list the objects, tools and moments a visitor actually sees in this business (a bakery: loaves, the oven, flour; an optician: frames, lenses, the test chart). The first screen must show the most characteristic of them as authored art at scale, so a stranger can name the business with the text covered. Then write down 3 concrete references from the brand's own world (local architecture, craft traditions, signage, landscape, the material itself) and derive palette, pattern, and type voice from them. The clichés below are generic *treatments* (layouts, kits, palettes), not the subject's own objects: avoid the treatments, never the subject.

matched_styles.name: Swiss Editorial Grid
characteristics: Exposed structural grid borders (`1px solid`) with generous internal cell padding
High-contrast serif or neo-grotesque display headlines paired with crisp body copy
Asymmetric column ratios (e.g., 4:8 or 5:7) with clear typographic hierarchy

matched_styles.name: Atelier Tactile Minimalism
characteristics: Warm paper and limestone neutrals (`#FAF8F5`) rather than sterile `#FFFFFF`
Unhurried vertical rhythm (`96px–140px` section spacing) and monograph captions
Zero decorative card wrappers; imagery and typography sit directly on the canvas

directions.title: Direction A — Artisan, Craft & Maker Commerce (Kit of Parts)
directions.layout_composition: Precision machine repair workshop as a kit of parts: the part on the stand shown finished at the centre, its parts laid out around it and labelled with material and size (part numbers, torque values and job tickets); the tool wall and the job ticket follow; 'book a repair slot' beside the finished object. Structure: parts laid out flat and labelled around the finished object. Knobs: density standard; span irregularity medium; accent on the selected option and the primary button. Mobile: the finished object first, the labelled parts list under it
directions.visual_identity: Exploded view: Helvetica for part names, Helvetica for sizes, Helvetica for notes; palette brand-ffffff-111111-666666-on-material-derived (light ground): brief colours #ffffff, #111111, #666666 lead: #ffffff is the ground; #666666 as accents; #111111 as surfaces and deep tones, never accents; corners: 2px on controls and cards, square images (hairline-2); body 1rem (16px) minimum, labels and captions 0.75rem (12px) minimum

typography.mood: The brief's own type (Helvetica); scale and roles from bricolage-hanken

palette.notes: Brief colours #FFFFFF, #111111, #666666 lead: #FFFFFF is the ground; #666666 as accents; #111111 as surfaces and deep tones, never accents | base Starting point only: replace accents with colours sampled from the maker's own materials, glazes, dyes, or place (see `distinctiveness`)

directions.content_treatment: What it is made of and why (part numbers, torque values and job tickets)
directions.motion_choreography: No motion: the part on the stand and every section render in their final state on load; hover and focus change colour only; nothing moves on scroll
directions.rationale: Kit of Parts for "precision machine repair workshop" (general surface): the product is assembled from parts, and showing them laid out builds trust in the whole. Type Helvetica / Helvetica and palette brand-ffffff-111111-666666-on-material-derived are the Artisan, Craft & Maker Commerce profile's own. First screen: object-wrap composition, hero material object, look family swiss-grid, corners hairline-2. Motion flavour (tier and tools follow page_shape.motion): parts assemble on scroll. Brand first: palette built around the brief's colours (#FFFFFF, #111111, #666666). Brand first: Helvetica is a commercial face: self-host it under the brand's own licence; it is not linked to a free CDN. Brand first: type built from the brief's fonts (Helvetica). hero_frame.build: One object centre-stage at large scale; type tucked around or behind it.

flow.build: Sticky index on one side; content panes scroll past it on the other side. The index is never an empty column: it carries the section titles plus the live picture or figure of the pane in view, and under 1024px it folds into a top bar.

section_head.build: Each head is a visitor's question in plain words; the answer starts right below.

ground.build: Alternate ground and ink sections: palette background, then the foreground colour as ground.

material.build: Photographic art direction: real-looking scenes of people, places and the work.

labels.build: A short accent dash before each label, body face semibold, sentence case.

motion.build: Micro motion only: hover, focus and press states (150-200ms), no scroll choreography; signature: focus-draw (CSS transitions). Reduced motion: under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every effect is replaced by its final state; all content stays visible and readable.

motion_techniques.build: Focus rings draw around controls in 150ms.

motif.build: Ruled frame: every chapter opens on a hairline rule with a short thick start segment, drawn from the trim lines of the part on the stand; figures and captions hang from the rule, which never crosses media.

button.build: Primary: solid accent fill, 48px tall with 24px side padding, radius 2px, label at medium weight; hover deepens the fill one step (150ms), press sinks it 1px, and keyboard focus shows a 2px accent ring offset 3px. Secondary: a button of the same size and radius with a 1px ink outline that fills on hover.

restraint: No eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, and no tiny tracked caps anywhere.
No monospace face: figures use the body face's tabular numerals.
No index numerals (01, 02) on sections or steps; an ordered list carries order.
No gradients, glows, glass panels or blobs: flat colour chapters carry the page.
No icon cards and no row of three or more identical cards: vary size, span and media per item.
At most two typefaces; hierarchy comes from size and weight.
One h1, authored in at most two lines at every width; statements stay under about 25 words.
Sections 120-240px apart on desktop (about clamp(88px, 11vw, 168px)); never cramped bands.
Real pictures of the trade's objects wherever the brief supplies them, four or more; no stock filler or placeholder art.
One live interaction born from the product (its deciding spec made interactive) with a no-JS table of the same facts.
The footer returns the brand line large across the full width.

workflow_guidance: BRIEF FONTS: the brief names its own type (Helvetica). Build every direction's type system from these (display and body roles among them; a mono role only where the restraint allows one); the direction pairings below are fallbacks only.
BRIEF COLOURS: the brief names its own colours (#FFFFFF, #111111, #666666). Use them as the palette in every direction (check WCAG pairs); the direction palettes below are fallbacks only.

Mode A (New Website): the user's prompt wins over everything here. The 3 directions are structural raw material (layout, content treatment, dials), not finished looks; the visual world comes from art direction.

DISTINCTIVENESS: Read `distinctiveness` first. If `match_confidence` is `none` or `weak`, the industry profile is only a fallback; build the visual world from the brief's place and material cues instead, and do not ship any listed category cliché unless the brief asks for it.

ART DIRECTION (load `skills/layoza-art-direction`): commit to ONE specific world. Derive the world from far (place, notation, print traditions), keep the subject up close (the trade's object as the signature interaction, at scale), rule out the category reflex and its obvious opposite, and put the visitor's real action in the first viewport. Let colour own whole sections. Decide motion and tools per design; nothing is mandatory.

ENGINEERING LESSONS: sticky headers need `html { scroll-padding-top: <header height + 1rem> }` (WCAG 2.4.11); web fonts need metric-adjusted fallback `@font-face` (size-adjust / ascent-override) or the font swap re-wraps headings and fails CLS; scroll reveals must end visible.

HERO: Layoza does not fix the first-screen composition; you choose it, from the subject and the brief. The directions suggest object-wrap / layered / full-bleed (each with its reason in `rationale`), and the dealt hero mechanic is one fit for that composition, not the only one. Give the three directions three different first screens, do not default to headline-left / visual-right (a split needs a stated reason), and record `HERO:` with the reason in `.layoza/direction.md`.
TYPE & LEADING: Keep multi-line display headings at `line-height >= 1.0` so ascenders and descenders never collide.

LAYOUT SAFETY: Keep short header links/buttons on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), give side-by-side heading columns >= 16px of clear space, collapse multi-column grids before gaps exceed the viewport, and size any <canvas> from a fixed-size container with devicePixelRatio capped at 2.
Verify in a real browser with `layoza qa <file-or-url>` (1440/768/375): it measures contrast, overflow, clipping, nav, scroll reveals, and lab Core Web Vitals; fix every error.

DIRECTIONS: render three materially different compositions with identical factual content and available assets at desktop and phone sizes. Compare the actual renders for hierarchy, typography, image integration, clarity and full-page rhythm. Choose with reasons as the designer unless the user asked to choose. Persist candidates, screenshot evidence and visible tradeoffs with review_design; never invent user approval. Library deals are starting material, not mandatory shapes or a substitute for art direction.

PAGE SHAPE: each direction's `page_shape` is a set of suggestions, not orders. Decide every axis (hero frame, flow, section heads, ground, material, labels, motion level and tools) from this brief's facts; keep a suggestion only when it serves your concept, and record each decision with its reason in .layoza/direction.md. Axes in `pinned_by_prompt` follow the user's words; whatever you choose stays unique against the ledger.

FORM: for each page or section answer narrative role, viewing distance, visual temperature, content capacity and visual motif before styling it; at delivery add one line per section saying which content the form came from.

COPY: specific nouns from the brief, no startup clichés, no invented metrics, reviews or logo walls (use honest placeholders such as `[customer quote — to supply]`), and call-to-action verbs taken from what the visitor actually does.

SELF-CRITIQUE before QA: score philosophy, hierarchy, execution, specificity, restraint, variety from 1 to 5; any score below 3 means revise first. Put the stamp `/* layoza · direction: <A|B|C> · structure: <style_family> · hero: <hero id> · palette: <palette id> · type: <type id> · critique: P4 H4 E4 S4 R4 V4 */` as the first line of the main CSS (your direction, structure, hero, palette, type and scores).

concepts.composition: Booking-first board for the precision machine repair workshop: date and time slots (with party size where it applies) working above the fold, stacked over today's board (the part on the stand, the tool wall, with prices or availability); location, hours and access follow as a ruled table. Structure: slots above the fold over today's board; location and hours as a ruled table. Knobs: density standard; span irregularity low; accent on links and the primary action. Mobile: slots become a horizontal day strip and a 2-column time grid with 48px targets
concepts.why_this_subject: Booking-First Board for "precision machine repair workshop" (general surface): most visitors arrive to book or check availability, often on a phone. Type Helvetica / Helvetica (the brief's own type (helvetica); scale and roles from chivo-workshop) for a utility voice, tagged industrial like the brief. Palette brand-ffffff-111111-666666-on-paper-signal-red on a light ground, tagged industrial like the brief. First screen: full-bleed composition (no fitting stacked hero for this trade, so the direction follows the dealt hero hero-slow-pan-band), hero material document, look family retro-print, corners ticket-notch. Motion flavour (tier and tools follow page_shape.motion): slot-selection micro-interactions. Brand first: palette built around the brief's colours (#FFFFFF, #111111, #666666). Brand first: Helvetica is a commercial face: self-host it under the brand's own licence; it is not linked to a free CDN. Brand first: type built from the brief's fonts (Helvetica). Other structures that fit this slot: Seasonal Almanac, Card Stack.

client_request: A precision machine repair workshop for local manufacturers. Show supported machine types and a repair enquiry. White and black only, Helvetica only, no animation, no invented accreditation.
craft_floor: Header: one row, 60-96px tall on desktop and 56-76px on mobile; logo 24-40px high on the left, 4-6 nav links of 15-16px at weight 500 with 24-40px between them, the primary action on the right at the header's button size. Phone or hours sit in that row or the footer; no utility bar stacked above the nav. Mark the current link with a 2px underline 6px below the text; a sticky header turns opaque after the first scroll, never taller.

Primary button: 44-60px tall, horizontal padding 20-32px (about twice the vertical), label 15-17px at weight 600 in sentence or title case with tracking 0-0.02em, at most one drawn SVG icon of 16-20px set 8px from the label. The secondary action matches its height, radius and padding as an outline (1-1.5px) or ghost; one button shape and radius on the whole page, 44px minimum hit area everywhere.

Button states, all four authored: :hover shifts the fill by 6-10% lightness or nudges the icon 2-4px; :active presses with translateY(1px) or scale(0.98) over 80-120ms; :focus-visible draws a 2px ring at 2-3px offset with at least 3:1 contrast; disabled sits at 45-55% opacity with cursor not-allowed. No state changes width, height or padding.

Type scale: at most 9 distinct font sizes each carry 2% or more of the text on a desktop render, each step at least 1.2x the one below; body 17-20px at line-height 1.5-1.65; headings at line-height 1.0-1.15. The h1 tops out at 120px on desktop (set with clamp()), and display sizes of 48px and up track -0.02 to -0.04em, never tighter than -0.05em; body text keeps tracking at 0.
Measure: prose never runs past 76 characters a line (cap paragraphs at 60-68ch with max-width); h1 lines stay under 20ch and h2 under 24ch; no centred paragraph runs past three lines.

Spacing rhythm: every gap comes from one 4/8px scale. Sections pad 88-168px top and bottom on desktop and 64-96px on mobile; a heading sits 16-24px above its text and has at least twice that space above it; content width caps at 1200-1320px with 24-40px gutters on desktop and 16-20px on mobile.

Section heads: one heading per section (one h2, or the h1 in the hero) and at most one lead paragraph of 40 words or fewer. No stacked pile of label, heading, accent-coloured second heading and paragraph; a second voice goes in the body, not the head.

Composition: no two neighbouring sections share a layout; use 4 or more layout kinds across the page (split, full-bleed media, list or table, asymmetric grid, quote, form). Card rows vary span or media; never a grid of equal cards that differ only by text.

Hero: the h1, one supporting paragraph of 30 words or fewer, at most two actions and one real picture or film; at most 14 text blocks in the first viewport. Spec tables, chip rows and stat grids go below the fold (one slim proof strip may sit on the fold line). On a 390x844 phone a real picture is in view before the first scroll.

Imagery: real photographs or renders of the trade's own objects, one aspect ratio per row (16:9, 3:2, 4:3 or 1:1) with object-fit: cover, corner radius from the button's family. Nothing decorative over a product picture: no hairlines, crosshairs, hotspot squares or graph-paper grids. Text on a photo sits on a scrim that holds 4.5:1; captions 13-14px in the muted ink.

Colour: one accent on no more than about 10% of any screen (primary action, links, one highlight); neutrals tinted toward the accent hue, never pure grey; at most two ground colours plus one accent ground across the page; body and secondary text at 4.5:1 or better, large text at 3:1.

Icons: one drawn SVG set at one stroke weight (1.5 or 2px) and one size per context (16, 20 or 24px), coloured with currentColor. Never a Unicode arrow, check mark, star or emoji standing in for an icon.

Motion: one signature moment; every other transition runs 200-450ms ease-out on transform and opacity only. Reveals travel 24px or less, start from content that is already readable, and differ by section role rather than one fade-up everywhere. No infinite loops besides hero media; prefers-reduced-motion turns all of it off.

Footer: brand and one-line description, two or three link groups and the contact block, four columns at most on desktop; group titles 13-14px at weight 600 in sentence case; links 15-16px with 10-12px between rows; a bottom bar for legal and copyright at 13-14px; 64px or more of top padding.

Browser surfaces: ::selection and focus rings use the palette; link underlines sit 3-4px below the text at 1-2px thickness; tables and figures use tabular numerals; no unthemed default blue links anywhere.

Craft: warm photography of hands, materials and the place in natural light, 3 or more real pictures above the footer, no stock; type with some character in the headings and a plain body; prices and opening hours are text, not images.

Corporate: the quote or contact action is reachable from every screen (header button plus one per long section), proof (client names, numbers with their source) sits within the first 2 scrolls (about 1800px).
